gaps.sentence: She took an evening job ___ fund her law degree.
gaps.explanation: 'In order to' + bare infinitive expresses purpose after a noun phrase subject.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: ___ fast you run, the train won't wait for you.
He spends money ___ it grew on trees.
gaps.explanation: 'As if it grew on trees' — the unreal comparison justifies the criticism.

gaps.sentence: She took notes during the seminar ___ she could write it up that evening.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.
